description: Hi I am Aaryan R Nair , student at CET..
summary: PERIHELION is an spacecraft design game built in Python and pygame. Players choose one of six science missions, from the Moon to the edge of the heliosphere. They then design a spacecraft by selecting structure, propulsion, power, communications, thermal protection, instruments, launch vehicle and orbit. A live engineering dashboard shows how each choice affects mass, delta-v, power, data and cost. A Mission Design Lab, inspired by NASA’s Mission Design Lab and JPL’s Concept Maturity Levels, rates how mature the design is from CML 1 to 4 and lets players compare candidate designs in a trade study. The game then runs a launch simulation and ends with a debrief that explains why the mission succeeded or failed, scores the design out of 1000, and names similar real NASA missions. PERIHELION makes systems engineering approachable by showing that every mission is a set of trade-offs, showcases how real missions are conceived.
details:
PERIHELION is a spacecraft design game. The player picks one of six science missions (Moon, Mars, Europa, an asteroid, Earth observation or deep space). They then choose parts, instruments, a launch vehicle and an orbit. A live dashboard recalculates mass, delta-v, power, data and cost using real relationships like the rocket equation and inverse-square falloff. The design is rated from “Not Feasible” to “Ready for Launch”, then launched in an animated simulation. A debrief explains the result, scores it out of 1000 and names similar real NASA missions. A Mission Design Lab, based on NASA’s Mission Design Lab and Concept Maturity Levels, rates each design from CML 1 to 4 and lets players compare three candidate designs in a trade study.

What benefits does it have?

Players see cause and effect immediately and learn from plain-language explanations of failures. Outcomes are deterministic, so improvement comes from reasoning, not luck.

What is the intended impact?

It makes systems engineering approachable, shows how real missions go from idea to design, and builds interest in space careers.

What tools and languages were used?

Python 3 with pygame, plus the standard math module. All visuals are drawn in code. The project has two files: engine.py for the model and astrocraft.py for the interface. It was built with VSCode and Google Antigravity, and runs on any ordinary computer.

How is it creative?

It turns a documents-and-spreadsheets process into a playable game. One engine drives the dashboard, report, simulation and trade study, and CML levels act as a progression system. Failure is treated as a lesson.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Accuracy vs simplicity: realistic formulas that stay easy to follow.
  • Clarity: short explanations on every part and a help screen.
  • Fairness: scoring rewards efficient trade-offs, not expensive parts.
  • Accessibility: mouse only control and text labels alongside colors.
  • Scope: six missions and one NASA resource, so it could be finished and tested.
